items.title: Protesters rally in Tel Aviv against Israeli government ahead of general election
items.original_title: Israel: Demonstrators rally against government ahead of election
items.continuity_note: Not included in the recent archived briefings.
items.summary: Thousands of demonstrators gathered in Tel Aviv on Friday to protest against the Israeli government ahead of an upcoming vote. The demonstration took place just three days before a national general election. The anti-government mobilization comes as the election is widely regarded as a referendum on Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
items.why: The large-scale public demonstrations signal heightened political tension as citizens cast ballots in a vote focused on top leadership.

items.title: Corporate and startup artificial intelligence projects face rising abandonments and shutdowns
items.original_title: The AI graveyard: a running list of projects and startups that didn’t make it
items.continuity_note: Not included in the recent archived briefings.
items.summary: A growing number of standalone artificial intelligence startups and products are shutting down or filing for bankruptcy. Market data indicates that approximately 42 percent of corporate artificial intelligence initiatives are ultimately abandoned by parent organizations. Major technology platforms are increasingly incorporating specialized capabilities directly into their main products, reducing demand for independent tools.
items.why: High operational costs, strong competition, and feature integration by major tech platforms make sustaining standalone hardware and software tools difficult.

items.title: NASA ends long-running Swift space observatory mission as orbit decays
items.original_title: NASA’s Swift Mission Ends, Leaves Behind Scientific Bonanza
items.continuity_note: Not included in the recent archived briefings.
items.summary: NASA’s Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory ended its science mission on October 20, 2026, after its orbit dropped below 171 miles above Earth. Atmospheric drag at this low altitude prevents the spacecraft's telescopes from stably pointing at astronomical targets, and re-entry is anticipated within weeks. Launched in 2004 for a planned two-year study of gamma-ray bursts, the satellite operated for nearly 22 years and compiled a 12-terabyte public archive.
items.why: Swift's rapid automated re-pointing enabled the first X-ray afterglow detection of short gamma-ray bursts, confirming that they originate from merging neutron stars.
technical_details: The spacecraft used co-aligned Optical/Ultraviolet and X-ray telescopes to rapidly refine burst positions.
Its flexible planning system could command ground-driven target-of-opportunity observations in minutes and schedule up to 75 independent targets daily.
items.corroboration: Single substantive source; independent corroboration not established.
items.display_title: NASA ends long-running Swift space observatory mission as orbit decays

items.title: Federal government halts evidence sharing in fatal Minnesota officer shootings
items.original_title: Trump administration stopped sharing evidence in Good and Pretti killings, Minnesota officials say
items.continuity_note: Not included in the recent archived briefings.
items.summary: Minnesota state officials stated in court filings that the federal government paused sharing evidence regarding the fatal shootings of Renee Good and Alex Pretti by federal officers. State prosecutors requested court orders for withheld evidence, including interview recordings, firearms, and the cell phone of the officer who killed Good. Justice Department attorneys argued that internal regulations allow them to withhold information, as no active formal court proceeding was underway when requests were made.
items.why: The halt in evidence sharing deepens jurisdictional disputes between state prosecutors seeking independent investigations and federal authorities asserting jurisdiction over federal officers.
items.selection_reason: Reports Minnesota state officials suing federal authorities over withheld evidence regarding fatal shootings by federal officers.
items.corroboration: Single substantive source; independent corroboration not established.
items.display_title: Federal government halts evidence sharing in fatal Minnesota officer shootings

items.title: Brazil votes in presidential runoff between Lula da Silva and Flavio Bolsonaro
items.original_title: What to know as Brazilians choose between Lula and Bolsonaro in tense presidential runoff
items.continuity_note: Not included in the recent archived briefings.
items.summary: Brazilians voted in a runoff presidential election between incumbent President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and Senator Flavio Bolsonaro. The first round concluded with Senator Bolsonaro securing 47 percent of the vote compared to Lula's 45 percent, leading to a closely contested final vote. Lula has focused his platform on resource sharing and labor reforms, while Bolsonaro advocates hard-line crime policies and megaprisons.
items.why: The outcome dictates Brazil's alignment with U.S. foreign policy, economic tariffs, and global environmental initiatives regarding Amazon rainforest protection.
items.selection_reason: Reports on the presidential election runoff in Brazil between Lula da Silva and Flavio Bolsonaro.
items.corroboration: Single substantive source; independent corroboration not established.
items.display_title: Brazil votes in presidential runoff between Lula da Silva and Flavio Bolsonaro

Speaking to reporters after voting, the President stated that he voted a straight Republican ticket and commented on various political races and foreign conflicts.
items.why: The midterm elections serve as a major test for the administration's leadership and control of Congress amid active political campaigns across the country.

items.title: Palestinians in Gaza face uncertainty amid Israeli elections
items.original_title: ‘Gaza’s suffering has become campaign fodder’: Palestinians fear the worst from Israel election
authors: Seham Tantesh in Gaza and Lorenzo Tondo
items.continuity_note: Not included in the recent archived briefings.
items.summary: As Israel prepares for elections, Palestinians in Gaza are bracing for the outcome while dealing with severe humanitarian conditions and ongoing military strikes. Political rivals Gadi Eisenkot and Benjamin Netanyahu have both vowed to end Hamas rule, while the broader humanitarian crisis in the territory remains largely absent from the campaign discourse.
items.why: The electoral outcome in Israel directly shapes the future and security of displaced Palestinians surviving in the heavily damaged enclave.
items.corroboration: Single substantive source; independent corroboration not established.
items.display_title: Palestinians in Gaza face uncertainty amid Israeli elections
